paper_notes: Vector addition is a streaming memory-bound primitive in PrIM.
Matrix-vector multiplication has lower data reuse than matrix-matrix multiplication.
Sparse matrix-vector multiplication combines low reuse with indirect memory access.
Select scans data and applies simple predicates.
Unique is data-movement-heavy and comparison-oriented.
Binary search has irregular access and low arithmetic work per memory access.
Time-series analytics uses simple operations over large arrays.
BFS is graph traversal with irregular memory access and low arithmetic intensity.
MLP appears in PrIM as a memory-bound neural-network workload on the evaluated baseline.
Needleman-Wunsch performs dynamic-programming updates with significant memory movement.
Small-bin histogram performs simple updates over image-like input data.
Large-bin histogram increases memory footprint and update pressure.
Reduction is a bandwidth-sensitive parallel primitive.
Scan variant from PrIM with synchronization and streaming memory behavior.
Scan variant from PrIM with reduction/scan phases.
Transpose stresses memory movement and access layout.
Compute-heavy tiled GEMM is a negative control because data reuse is high and arithmetic intensity is high.
Convolution is usually better served by GPU tensor/compute throughput than simple near-memory execution.
FFT has substantial arithmetic and communication structure that weakens simple PIM offloading.
Sorting is a negative control because communication and data rearrangement overhead can dominate.
